summary: pair sw/kk ignores the `threebody off` setting and always executes the O(jnum^2) three-body loop (results stay correct only because read_file zeroes lambda).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_sw_kokkos.cpp:418-422 `// there is no support for skipping threebody loops (yet) / bool tmp_threebody = skip_threebody_flag; skip_threebody_flag = false; PairSW::init_style(); skip_threebody_flag = tmp_threebody;` and compute() (lines 322-370) runs the jj/kk loop unconditionally, whereas src/MANYBODY/pair_sw.cpp:170-174 sets `jnumm1 = 0` when skip_threebody_flag. Numbers remain right only because src/MANYBODY/pair_sw.cpp:439 `if (skip_threebody_flag) params[nparams].lambda = 0;`.
failure_scenario: `pair_style sw/kk threebody off` runs the full three-body double loop with lambda=0, so sw/kk is several times slower than the CPU style for the same (two-body only) result.
suggested_fix: Guard the three-body loop with `if (!skip_threebody_flag)` (pass the flag into the functor), or at least skip the jj/kk loop when all lambda are zero.

summary: pair table/kk stores the special_lj weights into the inherited `int Pair::special_lj[4]`, truncating fractional special-bond factors (0.5 -> 0), so 1-2/1-3/1-4 pair interactions are silently dropped.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:124-127 `special_lj[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ... special_lj[3] = force->special_lj[3];`. PairTableKokkos (src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.h) declares NO special_lj member and src/pair_table.h has none either, so the name resolves to src/pair.h:247 `int special_lj[4];    // copied from force->special_lj for Kokkos` (force->special_lj is `double[4]`, src/force.h:116). Every other KOKKOS pair style shadows it with its own `KK_FLOAT special_lj[4]` (e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_soft_kokkos.h:89, src/KOKKOS/pair_morse_kokkos.h:90). The functor then reads it: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:181 `evdwl = factor_lj * c.template compute_evdwl<...>` with `factor_lj = c.special_lj[j >> SBBITS & 3]`.
failure_scenario: `special_bonds lj 0.0 0.0 0.5` + `pair_style table/kk linear N`: force->special_lj[3]=0.5 is stored as int 0, so all 1-4 tabulated pair interactions get factor 0 instead of 0.5 -> wrong forces and energies, silently. The CPU pair_style table gives 0.5. Any non-integer weight (0.5, 0.8333, ...) is affected.
suggested_fix: Declare `KK_FLOAT special_lj[4];` as a member of PairTableKokkos (as every other KOKKOS pair style does), or change src/pair.h:247 to `double special_lj[4];`.

summary: PairTableKokkos::settings() releases the cutsq/tabindex dual views but never frees the aliased legacy row-pointer arrays, leaking them and leaving `cutsq`/`tabindex` dangling and non-null.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:469-477 `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); d_table_const.tabindex = d_table->tabindex = typename AT::t_int_2d_lr(); h_table->tabindex = HAT::t_int_2d_lr(); d_table_const.cutsq = d_table->cutsq = typename AT::t_double_2d_lr(); h_table->cutsq = HAT::t_double_2d_lr(); }`. The arrays were made by `memoryKK->create_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,h_table->cutsq,cutsq,nt,nt,...)` (line 420), which `smalloc`s an `n1`-entry row-pointer array (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:186-196) that only `destroy_kokkos(TYPE&, value_type**&)` (memory_kokkos.h:297-306) frees and nulls. The CPU base does it properly: src/pair_table.cpp settings() `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); memory->destroy(cutsq); memory->destroy(tabindex); }`.
failure_scenario: Repeated `pair_style table/kk ...` commands in one input leak the row-pointer arrays each time and leave `cutsq`/`tabindex` pointing at freed view memory; any read of `cutsq[i][j]` before the next `allocate()` is use-after-free.
suggested_fix: Replace the manual view resets with `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,cutsq);` and `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->tabindex,tabindex);` (then also reset the host mirrors), matching the destructor at lines 62-63.

summary: Global vdW energy is accumulated under `if (eflag)` rather than `if (eflag_global)`, so eng_vdwl is polluted on steps that request only per-atom energy.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.cpp:177 `if (eflag) eng_vdwl += static_cast<double>(ev.evdwl);` while line 178 correctly uses `if (vflag_global)`. src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:180-183 accumulates `ev.evdwl` whenever `c.eflag_either` is set (i.e. also for eflag==2/atom-only), and Pair::ev_setup only zeroes eng_vdwl when eflag_global is set.
failure_scenario: A step where only `compute pe/atom` is invoked (eflag==2, eflag_global==0) adds the full pair energy into eng_vdwl without ever resetting it; any consumer reading Pair::eng_vdwl before the next eflag_global step sees a doubled/stale value.
suggested_fix: Use `if (eflag_global) eng_vdwl += ...` as the other 59 KOKKOS pair styles do.

summary: On steps with eflag==0 && vflag==0, pair table/rx/kk writes uCG/uCGnew on the device but marks only F_MASK modified, so the device updates are silently discarded by the next host sync.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:670-671 `if (eflag || vflag) atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify); else atomKK->modified(execution_space,F_MASK);` while the kernel writes uCG/uCGnew unconditionally: lines 527-531 `uCG_i += 0.5*evdwlOld; if (do_half) uCG(j) += ...; uCGnew_i += 0.5*evdwl; ...` and lines 546-547 `uCG(i) += uCG_i; uCGnew(i) += uCGnew_i;` (no EVFLAG guard). The two sibling RX pair styles get it right: src/KOKKOS/pair_exp6_rx_kokkos.cpp:151-152 and src/KOKKOS/pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.cpp:238-239 both keep `UCG_MASK | UCGNEW_MASK` in the `else` branch.
failure_scenario: A normal MD step (no thermo/dump output, eflag=vflag=0) with `pair_style table/rx/kk` + `fix eos/table/rx/kk`: the fix does `atomKK->sync(Host,UCG_MASK|UCGNEW_MASK)` (src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:290) which is a no-op because the dual view was never marked device-modified, then `modified(Host,...)` (line 292) and `sync(execution_space,...)` (line 294) copy the stale host values back over the device -> the pair style's uCG/uCGnew contributions are lost and the internal-energy/reaction integration is wrong on every non-output step.
suggested_fix: Change the else branch to `atomKK->modified(execution_space, F_MASK | UCG_MASK | UCGNEW_MASK);`, matching pair_exp6_rx_kokkos and pair_multi_lucy_rx_kokkos.

summary: The special-bond LJ weights are stored in a `Few<int,4>`, truncating fractional special_bonds factors (0.5 -> 0) and dropping those pair interactions.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:679-683 `Few<int, 4> special_lj_local; special_lj_local[0] = force->special_lj[0]; ... special_lj_local[3] = force->special_lj[3];` (force->special_lj is `double[4]`, src/force.h:116). The functor signature keeps the int type (line 425 `Few<int, 4> const& special_lj`, line 570) and line 477 reads it: `const KK_FLOAT factor_lj = special_lj[sbmask(j)];`. The CPU base uses the double array directly: src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:94 `double *special_lj = force->special_lj;` and line 144 `factor_lj = special_lj[sbmask(j)];`.
failure_scenario: `special_bonds lj 0.0 0.0 0.5` with `pair_style table/rx/kk`: 1-4 pairs get factor_lj = int(0.5) = 0 instead of 0.5, so those tabulated interactions (force, energy and the uCG/uCGnew contributions, all of which are multiplied by factor_lj) vanish. Silent wrong answer vs. the CPU style.
suggested_fix: Change `Few<int, 4>` to `Few<KK_FLOAT, 4>` (or `Few<double,4>`) in the local variable at line 679 and in the `compute_item`/`compute_all_items` signatures (lines 425, 570).

summary: PairTableRXKokkos::settings() releases the cutsq/tabindex dual views without freeing the aliased legacy row-pointer arrays, leaking them and leaving `cutsq`/`tabindex` dangling.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:1038-1047 `if (allocated) { memory->destroy(setflag); d_table_const.tabindex = d_table->tabindex = typename ArrayTypes<DeviceType>::t_int_2d_lr(); h_table->tabindex = ...; d_table_const.cutsq = d_table->cutsq = ...; h_table->cutsq = ...; allocated = 0; }`. Those arrays came from `memoryKK->create_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,h_table->cutsq,cutsq,nt,nt,...)` (line 985), which smallocs an nt-entry row-pointer array (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:186-196) freed only by `destroy_kokkos(TYPE&, value_type**&)`. The CPU base frees them: src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:286-290 `memory->destroy(setflag); memory->destroy(cutsq); memory->destroy(tabindex);`.
failure_scenario: Repeated `pair_style table/rx/kk ...` commands leak the row-pointer arrays and leave `cutsq`/`tabindex` non-null but pointing into released view memory.
suggested_fix: Use `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->cutsq,cutsq);` and `memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_table->tabindex,tabindex);` instead of the manual view resets.

summary: getMixingWeights asserts `isite1 >= 0` / `isite2 >= 0`, which is false for the legal `1fluid` setting (OneFluidValue == -1), so debug builds abort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:90-93 `assert(isite1 >= 0); assert(isite1 < nspecies); assert(isite2 >= 0); assert(isite2 < nspecies);` but line 50 `#define OneFluidValue (-1)` and lines 94/103/113 explicitly handle `isOneFluid(isite1)`; isite1/isite2 are set to OneFluidValue at lines 1161/1171 when the pair_coeff site name is "1fluid". The CPU base (src/DPD-REACT/pair_table_rx.cpp:504-593) has no such assertion.
failure_scenario: `pair_coeff 1 1 table file.table ENTRY 1fluid 1fluid` in a build without NDEBUG (any Debug/RelWithDebInfo-without-NDEBUG build, host or CUDA) aborts inside the kernel at the first timestep.
suggested_fix: Drop the two lower-bound asserts, or relax them to `assert(isOneFluid(isite1) || (isite1 >= 0 && isite1 < nspecies));`.

summary: Global vdW energy is accumulated under `if (eflag)` rather than `if (eflag_global)`, polluting eng_vdwl on per-atom-energy-only steps.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:810 `if (eflag) eng_vdwl += static_cast<double>(ev.evdwl);` while line 811 uses `if (vflag_global)`. `ev.evdwl` is accumulated unconditionally in the kernel (line 534) and Pair::ev_setup only zeroes eng_vdwl when eflag_global is set.
failure_scenario: A step where only `compute pe/atom` runs (eflag==2, eflag_global==0) adds the whole pair energy into eng_vdwl without a reset.

summary: The fused ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij() (the only bij derivative actually used by tersoff/kk) still contains the pre-2022 buggy extra 0.5 factor in the second term, so the bond-order prefactor differs from the CPU style and from the file's own unfused ters_dbij().
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:836-838 `prefactor = param.beta * (factor * (1.0 - 0.5*(1.0 + 0.5/(prm_ijk_pn)) * tmp_pow_neg_prm_ijk_pn));` versus the corrected unfused version in the same file, lines 802-807: `return param.beta * (factor * /* error in negligible 2nd term fixed 2/21/2022 */ /* (1.0 - 0.5*(1.0 + 1.0/(2.0*param.powern)) * */ (1.0 - (1.0 + 0.5/(param.powern)) * Kokkos::pow(tmp,-param.powern)));` and the CPU base src/MANYBODY/pair_tersoff.cpp ters_bij_d(): `return param->beta * (-0.5*pow(tmp,-1.5) * (1.0 - (1.0 + 1.0/(2.0*param->powern)) * pow(tmp,-param->powern)));`. Line 436 `ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij(d_params(iparam_ij),bo_ij,bij,prefactor);` is the call site; ters_dbij()/ters_bij_k() are dead code in this file. The sibling KOKKOS styles use the correct unfused form (pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:484, pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:441, pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp:446).
failure_scenario: Any tersoff/kk configuration where beta*zeta falls in the (c2, c1] branch (roughly 2*n*1e-16 < (beta*zeta)^-n < 2*n*1e-8) gets a three-body prefactor that is wrong by ~half of the correction term (~1e-8 relative), so tersoff/kk forces do not match pair_style tersoff bit-for-bit in that branch.
suggested_fix: Drop the extra `0.5*` so the fused branch reads `(1.0 - (1.0 + 0.5/prm_ijk_pn) * tmp_pow_neg_prm_ijk_pn)`, matching ters_dbij() and the CPU base.

summary: Dead device helpers left behind after the fusing rewrite: ters_bij_k, ters_dbij, ters_fa_k, ters_dfa, ters_dthbj, ters_dthbk and v_tally3_atom are never called.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp defines ters_bij_k (780), ters_dbij (797), ters_fa_k (737), ters_dfa (749), ters_dthbj (938), ters_dthbk (1001), v_tally3_atom (1162); grep for call sites in the file yields only the fused `ters_fa_k_and_ters_dfa` (435), `ters_bij_k_and_ters_dbij` (436) and `ters_fc_k_and_ters_dfc` (507). They are exactly the copies that drifted out of sync with the fused versions (see the ters_dbij finding).
failure_scenario: No runtime effect, but the duplicated formulas are what let the fused/unfused divergence go unnoticed.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused helpers (or make the fused versions call them) so there is a single copy of each formula.

summary: Error message names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk") in the tersoff/mod/c/kk (and mod, zbl) variants.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp:120-121 `if (neighflag == FULL) error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` - identical copy-pasted text in pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:121 and pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:134.
failure_scenario: A user running `pair_style tersoff/mod/c/kk` with `package kokkos neigh full` is told to fix `pair tersoff/kk`, a style that is not in their input.
suggested_fix: Use the real style name in each variant's message (tersoff/mod/c/kk, tersoff/mod/kk, tersoff/zbl/kk).

summary: pair snap/kk never strips the special-bond bits from the neighbor index (`j &= NEIGHMASK` is missing), so in a molecular system it dereferences out-of-range atom indices.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:554 `T_INT j = d_neighbors(i,jj);` then `x(j,0)`, `type(j)` (lines 555-559); again at 581 `T_INT j = d_neighbors(i,jj);` with `snaKK.inside(ii,offset) = j;` (line 591); and in the CPU path at 634 and 653. `grep -n NEIGHMASK src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h` returns nothing, while the CPU base does mask: src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:142-143 `j = jlist[jj]; j &= NEIGHMASK;` (also at 315-316), and sibling KOKKOS manybody styles do too (src/KOKKOS/pair_sw_kokkos.cpp:233-234, src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:350-351). The KOKKOS neighbor build really does set those bits: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:500 and :726 `neighbors_i(n++) = j ^ (which << SBBITS);` for `molecular != Atom::ATOMIC`.
failure_scenario: A molecular system (atom_style full/molecular) where Neighbor::init sets special_flag=2 - which src/neighbor.cpp:557-558 does for EVERY special weight as soon as a kspace_style is defined - run with `pair_style hybrid/overlay snap/kk ... coul/long/kk` : neighbor entries for 1-2/1-3/1-4 pairs carry the SBBITS, so snap/kk reads x/type at index j|(which<<30), i.e. far past the end of the per-atom views -> garbage rij/type, wrong forces or a segfault; the stored `snaKK.inside` index is then used for `a_f(j,*) -= fij[*]` (line 1382) writing out of bounds.
suggested_fix: Add `j &= NEIGHMASK;` immediately after every `d_neighbors(i,jj)` read in TagPairSNAPComputeNeigh and TagPairSNAPComputeNeighCPU (lines 554, 581, 634, 653).

summary: TagPairSNAPPreUi looks up the atom type with the chunk-relative index instead of the real atom index, so with chunking (inum > chunksize) it initializes ulisttot with the wrong element for chem-SNAP potentials.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:711-718 `const int iatom = iatom_mod + iatom_div * vector_length; if (iatom >= chunk_size) return; int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);` (same in the two other PreUi overloads, lines 724-731 and 736-744). Every other kernel in the same file converts first: e.g. line 534 `const int i = d_ilist[ii + chunk_offset];`, lines 986-988, 999-1001, 1012-1014, 1035-1037, 1048-1050, 1061-1063, 1365. `chunk_offset` is advanced by `chunk_offset += chunk_size;` (line 388) inside the chunking loop (line 191), and the KOKKOS neighbor build sets `d_ilist(i) = i` (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:593 etc.), so `type(iatom)` is the type of atom `iatom` rather than of atom `iatom + chunk_offset`. `ielem` selects the diagonal element block in SNAKokkos::pre_ui (src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h: `if (ma == mb && (!chem_flag || ielem == jelem || wselfall_flag)) { re_part = wself; }`).
failure_scenario: A chemflag SNAP potential (`chemflag 1`, wselfall off) with more than `chunksize` (default 32768, src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:636) local atoms per MPI rank: for every chunk after the first, `wself` is placed in the element block of the wrong atom, giving wrong bispectrum components, energies and forces. Silent - results simply differ from pair_style snap and from a smaller-chunksize run.
suggested_fix: In all three TagPairSNAPPreUi overloads, replace `type(iatom)` with `type(d_ilist[iatom + chunk_offset])`, matching TagPairSNAPComputeBetaLinear.

summary: The neighbor screening drops the CPU base's `rsq > 1e-20` guard, so a neighbor exactly on top of atom i enters the SNAP kernels with r == 0.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:562 `if (rsq >= rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype)) { jtype = -1; }` and line 642/662 `if (rsq < rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype))`, versus src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:151 `if (rsq < cutsq[itype][jtype]&&rsq>1e-20) {`. The same guard is present in every CPU ML-SNAP style (compute_sna_atom.cpp:417, compute_snad_atom.cpp:318, compute_snap.cpp:400, compute_snav_atom.cpp:314, pair_snap.cpp:324).
failure_scenario: Two coincident atoms (or a self-image in a box smaller than the cutoff) yield r = 0; the CPU style skips the pair, snap/kk divides by zero in compute_cayley_klein / compute_ui and produces NaN forces for the whole configuration.
suggested_fix: Add the `&& rsq > 1e-20` condition to the cutoff test in both TagPairSNAPComputeNeigh and TagPairSNAPComputeNeighCPU.
